text:
maria: Quick smoke thread — ran a tiny cross-arch sweep (L4/T4/A10 vs A100/H100) against nightly runtime with the new kernel-presets. Seeing surprising p99 regressions on L4 for long sequences (~2k+). @sam @yusuf can you eyeball the profiles?

sam: thanks — which preset did you use? balanced_seq or cost_saver?

maria: balanced_seq (we left --auto-kernel=on). baseline for L4 had p99 ~420ms at seq=2048; new run shows ~680ms and lower throughput. A100/H100 unchanged.

yusuf: sounds like we fell back to a non-optimal GEMM kernel for >1024. Did you collect kernel names from the trace?

maria: grabbed a quick perf trace. snippet: ```
2026-02-28 18:12:03 INFO kernel_pick: flash-attn-kernel-v2 selected for seq<=1024
2026-02-28 18:12:03 INFO kernel_pick: fused-gemm-small fallback selected for seq>1024
2026-02-28 18:12:04 METRIC p99_latency_ms=680
```

sam: fused-gemm-small is cheap on A100/H100 but on L4 it spikes due to extra memcpy and kernel grid inefficiency. We should prefer tiled-gemm-vec (tile=128) for L4 at 1k-4k ranges.

nina: what about KV cache path? if we hit kv-prefix-cache eviction we might be thrashing the small-L4 memory. Any evictions logged?

maria: yes we see incremental kv evict counts bumping at long seqs: kv_evictions=12 per request average. memory footprint ~3.2GB vs baseline ~2.4GB.

yusuf: that aligns — on L4 the per-request workspace + memcpy means the kernel choice matters more. Two action items: 1) add an L4-specific override in kernel-preset for seq buckets 1025-4096 to prefer tiled-gemm-vec, 2) disable aggressive kv re-allocation in that preset (kv-cache: prefer_static).

chris: pinging infra-bot to run a 6-run mini-job across device families with those overrides. infra-bot: can you run the sweep? :robot_face:

infra-bot: queued job 2147010001 — cross-arch-mini-sweep, configs: balanced_seq + l4_override_v1, tile=128, kv_policy=prefer_static. ETA ~20m. (logs will post here)

sam: also add a micro-benchmark: single-batch throughput tok/s vs seq 512/1024/2048, and record kernel names + shared_mem usage. We need to confirm no CUDA occupancy regression.

maria: agreed. I'll add the micro-bench harness: ```bash
# run micro-bench
python perf/run_micro.py --model redwood-7b --batch 1 --seq 2048 --device L4 --preset l4_override_v1 --collect-kernels
```

yusuf: if the tiled-gemm-vec helps on L4, we should add threshold into autotune: when observed p99_delta > 20% & device.family==L4 then pin kernel=tile128. That avoids platform-wide regressions.

nina: small note — for A10 we saw slightly higher memory pressure than T4 in past runs; ensure preset only targets L4 (and maybe T4) explicitly, not A10 unless validated.

maria: infra-bot posted partial logs: ```
[2147010100] L4 seq=2048 p99=435ms (l4_override_v1)
[2147010100] A100 seq=2048 p99=410ms
[2147010100] H100 seq=2048 p99=395ms
[2147010100] T4 seq=2048 p99=620ms
[2147010100] notes: kernel_names L4: tiled-gemm-vec; T4: fused-gemm-small; A100: flash-attn-kernel-v2
```

sam: interesting — override helped L4 (435ms vs 680ms), T4 still bad. Maybe T4 needs a different tile size (tile=64) or different launch params.

yusuf: propose two presets: l4_tile128 and t4_tile64, and a tiny device-family routing table. autotune should test both on device family and pick.

maria: created a draft preset files under runtime/configs/presets: l4_tile128_v1 and t4_tile64_v1 (will push PR). Quick question: should kv-policy be globally part of the preset or separate flag? Prefer separate so we can A/B test kv changes without touching kernel picks.

chris: separate flag sounds safer. we can label it kv_policy=prefer_static and do canary on 5% traffic.

nina: also record any increase in memcpy_time and kernel_launch_time from traces, that will help tune launch params.

maria: thanks all — next steps I will: 1) open PR with two presets and autotune thresholds, 2) run a 24h mini-sweep on devices with collect-kernels on, 3) write short runbook for fallback policy (if pinned kernel causes OOM, fallback to cost_saver).

yusuf: lgtm. leave the PR link here when ready and we can land after 1 more smoke. :thumbsup:
